task: Non-persistent merge rehearsal and semantic conflict analysis between Team S (58d33d9) and Team G (a50fa30)
observation: Simulating merge revealed that while text conflicts are cleanly isolated to 3 files, a subtle semantic interaction occurs between Team G's module-based field access visibility check (FIELD_VISIBILITY_ERROR) and project-mode compilation without an explicit 'module' header. specialization_calling_module returned empty string for functions without '__', comparing against p_.main_module and falsely rejecting same-package record field projections.
impact: Prevented unexpected breakage of Team S's check-display suite (check_phase25_sb_check_display.py) and other project-mode packages during final integration by identifying the exact fallback logic needed in specialization_calling_module and check_expression.
evidence: check_phase25_sb_check_display.py failed on Bag.xs projection in project mode with FIELD_VISIBILITY_ERROR
specialization_calling_module('fn:main') returned empty string rather than p_.main_module
Adding p_.main_module fallback restored 100% test pass rate across both Team S and Team G test suites

resolution.summary: Documented the root-module fallback in the integration playbook and conflict register so the final integration merge incorporates the fix cleanly.

tool_used: git merge-tree and python test harness
suggestion: Always run merge rehearsals with project-mode test suites as well as standalone tests, since module-qualification semantics diverge when a project manifest is present.
